sections.html:
The county offices share one address, 204 High Street in Marble Hill, Missouri 63764, and one main number, 573-238-1900. Ask for the Collector when you call about a bill and for the Assessor about a value.

Bollinger County offices at 204 High Street

TreasurerSuite 8, 573-238-1900

Marble Hill holds the courthouse and is the only city. Glen Allen, Sedgewickville and Zalma are villages. The county is split among four school districts: Woodland R-IV at Marble Hill, Leopold R-III, Meadow Heights R-II at Patton and Zalma R-V.

Bollinger County is rural throughout, with 10,567 people counted in 2020 across 618 square miles of land. The county is part of the Cape Girardeau metro area, and many residents commute a long way, with a mean travel time to work of 35.5 minutes. The buyer pool is small and local, made up of long-term owners, family transfers and buyers who accept a long drive.

  • Housing units in 2025: 5,045
  • Share of households that own, 2020-2024: 82.3 percent
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $179,800
  • Median gross rent: $694
  • Building permits in 2025: 0

With so little new construction, existing houses carry the market. For those buyers, a clean tax record and a prompt, well-documented closing are what keep a contract together.

sections.h2: When Bollinger County taxes are due
sections.html:
December 31 is the last day in every Missouri county, Bollinger included. After it, unpaid balances start picking up interest and penalties, and RSMo 139.100 counts a mailed payment as timely when its postmark falls inside the period. For bill timing, accepted payment types and the current mailing address, call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector.

Land that stays unpaid is hit by RSMo 140.100, which adds an 18 percent penalty on that year's delinquency, or no more than 2 percent a month if the owner redeems ahead of a sale. Sales are held on the fourth Monday in August.

sections.h2: How the Bollinger County tax sale works
sections.html:
RSMo 140.150 puts land with unpaid taxes or special assessments up for sale on the fourth Monday of each August. Owners get several safeguards first.

  • The collector must mail a first class notice to the recorded owner before delinquent land is published for sale.
  • A second notice by certified mail is required when the assessed value is above $1,000.
  • If the certified notice comes back unsigned, a further first class notice goes to the owner and to any occupant.
  • Tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the county collector at any time before the sale.

A notice that never reached you doesn't wipe out the tax. Moved recently? Give the Collector your new mailing address, since notices go to the owner of record.

Your first stop is the Assessor at 204 High Street, Suite 1, who values real and personal property every year and can walk you through the factors. If that doesn't settle it, file with the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July.

The state level is the Missouri State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 lets an owner take the board's ruling there, within the statutory time or 30 days after the board acts, whichever is later. File online, by email, or by mail to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102. Corporations, LLCs, trusts and estates must be represented by an attorney.

To argue about value without missing the payment deadline, pay under protest: send the full bill by December 31, mark the check, and give the Collector a written statement of the market value you claim.

Treat the tax bill as part of the price discussion. Real estate tax follows the land, so a buyer takes the property subject to anything unpaid. A title company will normally order a tax search, and you can head off surprises by calling the Collector for the balance and asking whether any prior year is open.

If the Assessor holds the wrong mailing address, or the legal description on file differs from the deed, correct it before listing. The Recorder in Suite 7 keeps the deed record, and the Treasurer in Suite 8 is a separate office from the Collector. Ask each one for its own instructions rather than assuming the same counter handles them all.

  1. Call the Collector and get the balance, including any older year.
  2. Fix any address or legal description problem with the Assessor.
  3. Give the payoff to the title company.
  4. Confirm the Recorder will file the deed after closing.

A cash buyer still runs the same tax search, though with no lender involved the closing can move as soon as the balance is cleared.

sections.h2: A Bollinger County calendar for sellers
sections.html:
Bills follow a fixed yearly rhythm, and it helps to know where your sale falls in it.

  • January 1: the owner of record on this date is billed for the year.
  • Second Monday in July: last day to file with the Board of Equalization.
  • September 30: general State Tax Commission filing limit, unless the board ruled late.
  • Fourth Monday in August: tax sale of delinquent land.
  • December 31: payment deadline and postmark cutoff.

A sale that closes in the fall leaves the buyer and seller to decide who pays the bill that arrives in the weeks before December 31. Put it in writing in the contract, and have the title company hold back the seller's share if the bill hasn't been issued yet. Whoever pays should keep the receipt.

A short call to 573-238-1900 saves problems later. Ask these before you list.

  • What is the balance on my parcel, and is any earlier year open?
  • Which mailing address do you have on file?
  • How do you accept payment, and what fee applies to each type?
  • Has the parcel ever been published for the August sale?

Get the answers in an email or note and pass them to the title company. If a bill is wrong because of value, that goes to the Assessor, not the Collector.

The state Property Tax Credit program refunds up to $750 to qualifying older or disabled residents whose household income stays under set limits and who paid real estate tax or rent on their home. The Missouri Department of Revenue runs it, at 573-751-3505, and the claim goes on Form MO-PTC. For a local senior freeze, ask the County Clerk at 573-238-1900.

faqs.q: What is the Bollinger County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, the statewide deadline. Call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector to confirm how and where to pay.

faqs.q: Where is the Bollinger County Assessor?
faqs.a: At 204 High Street, Suite 1, Marble Hill, MO 63764. The main number is 573-238-1900, extension 1 for the Assessor.

faqs.q: When is the Bollinger County tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in August under state law, every year.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes be paid before the sale?
faqs.a: Yes. RSMo 140.150 lets an owner pay the delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector at any time before the property is sold.

faqs.q: How many people live in Bollinger County?
faqs.a: About 10,646 in 2025, up 0.7 percent from 10,567 in 2020, spread across 618 square miles of land.
